line: At 14, strings snapped on two violins mid-concert. Midori never missed a note.
Strings snap. Joy and sorrow both come. Accept them with a calm, content mind.
The lesson? Prepare ahead, and there is nothing to worry about.
credit: 有備無患 · Chinese, Japanese, Korean idiom

line: An old Thai saying: buy a buffalo at ploughing time, and you pay more.
Start with the body: asana should be firm, and pleasant too.
Then the mind. Hancock hit a wrong chord. Miles breathed and made it right.
We suffer more often in our minds than in real life.
credit: Seneca · Letters to Lucilius 13, tr. Gummere

line: Almost daily, same place: in one study, habits like this went with less stress.
credit: Wood et al. · J Pers Soc Psychol, 2002

line: Yoga is 99 percent practice, 1 percent theory, Guruji said. So live it daily.
credit: R. Sharath Jois · Yoga Mala foreword, 2009

line: Sting: after morning yoga, more energy, more done, a calmer mind. Your turn tomorrow.
